name: Jakob
speaker: boy
personality: Six, the smallest of the village children, Müller Franz's grandson. Shy at first, then chatty; counts everything like his grandfather ('eins, zwei, drei!'), loves horses (the big Noriker), the tractor and bedtime stories. Says du to the learner and looks up to them like a big brother or sister. Very short sentences and simple words.
story: Jakob lives with his grandfather Franz by the field and follows him to work every morning. He knows every Noriker horse in the Gailtal by name, sits on the old red tractor pretending to drive it, and asks Opa Sepp for the Lindwurm story every evening.

greet.de: Hallo! Ich bin Jakob. Ich bin sechs.
greet.sl: Živjo! Jaz sem Jakob. Star sem šest let.
greet.it: Ciao! Io sono Jakob. Ho sei anni.

greet.de: Hallo! Willst du den Traktor sehen?
greet.en: Hi! Do you want to see the tractor?

greet.de: He! Ich habe die Pferde gezählt: drei!
greet.sl: Ej! Preštel sem konje: trije so!
greet.en: Hey! I counted the horses: there are three!
greet.it: Ehi! Ho contato i cavalli: sono tre!

greet.de: Juhu, du bist da! Spielst du mit mir?
greet.sl: Juhu, tu si! Se igraš z mano?
greet.en: Hooray, you're here! Will you play with me?
greet.it: Evviva, sei qui! Giochi con me?

greet.de: Mit dir ist es am schönsten! Komm, komm!
greet.sl: S tabo je najlepše! Pridi, pridi!
greet.en: It's the best with you! Come, come!
greet.it: Con te è più bello! Vieni, vieni!

thanks.de: Danke! Das sage ich dem Opa.

remember.de: Weißt du noch? Ich denke noch an {memory}!
remember.sl: Se spomniš? Jaz še vedno mislim na {memory}!
remember.en: Do you remember? I still think of {memory}!

idle.de: Eins, zwei, drei, vier … vier Hühner!
idle.sl: Ena, dve, tri, štiri … štiri kokoši!
idle.en: One, two, three, four … four hens!
idle.it: Uno, due, tre, quattro … quattro galline!

idle.de: Der Traktor vom Opa ist rot.
idle.it: Il trattore del nonno è rosso.

idle.de: Schau! Das Pferd frisst den Apfel.
idle.en: Look! The horse is eating the apple.
idle.it: Guarda! Il cavallo mangia la mela.

idle.de: Heute Abend erzählt Opa Sepp vom Lindwurm.
idle.sl: Nocoj bo dedek Sepp pripovedoval o zmaju Lindwurmu.
idle.en: Tonight Opa Sepp is telling the story of the Lindwurm (the dragon).
idle.it: Stasera Nonno Sepp racconta del Lindwurm, il drago.

comfort.de: Ich mache auch Fehler. Noch einmal!
comfort.sl: Tudi jaz se zmotim. Še enkrat!
comfort.en: I get it wrong too. Again!

listen.en: Shh … can you hear the horse?

bye.de: Tschüss! Ich gehe zu den Pferden.
bye.en: Bye! I'm going to see the horses.
bye.it: Ciao! Vado a vedere i cavalli.

bye.sl: Pfiat di! Se jutri igrava? (pfiat di: avstrijski pozdrav, adijo)
bye.en: Pfiat di! Shall we play tomorrow? (pfiat di: Austrian for bye)
bye.it: Pfiat di! Domani giochiamo? (pfiat di: saluto austriaco, ciao)

liked.de: Das mag ich! Eins, zwei … sooo sehr!
liked.sl: Všeč mi je! Ena, dva … zelo, zelo!
liked.en: I like it! One, two … so, so much!

liked.de: Woher weißt du das? Das sage ich dem Opa!
liked.en: How did you know? I'll tell Grandpa!
liked.it: Come lo sapevi? Lo dico al nonno!

ordinary.de: Danke! Ist das wirklich für mich?
ordinary.en: Thanks! Is it really for me?

rare.de: Wow! Wie schön! Danke, danke, danke!
rare.sl: Uau! Kako lepo! Hvala, hvala, hvala!
rare.en: Wow! How lovely! Thanks, thanks, thanks!
rare.it: Uau! Che bello! Grazie, grazie, grazie!
